title: Presidents of the United States, in order
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: Knowing the presidents in order gives American history a backbone. Each name becomes a hook to hang events on: wars, inventions, new states. It is a classic memory-work list, and it is long enough to show why chunking and spaced review matter.

How to hold it: Chunk first. Forty-seven names is far more than the four or so things the mind holds at once, so the list is split by era into groups of four to six. Learn one group, recall it with the book closed, then add the next. Old groups come back on day 1, 3, 7 and 21. For a stronger hook, walk a memory palace: Washington washing the front door, Adams with an apple in his throat on the mat, and so on, one picture per stop.
This list has 47 items. Answer below, then check — the practice button generates fresh questions from the list itself.
